Japan.name: Japan
Japan.basicInfo:
Japan, generations after the first Quirks appeared. Four in five people have one, registered by age four. Using a Quirk in public without a hero license is illegal except in self-defense or supervised training, so fighting villains falls to licensed heroes, certified by the Hero Public Safety Commission and employed by agencies. Twice a year the Hero Billboard Chart JP ranks them by incidents resolved, public approval and social contribution. At the start of the year All Might, the Number One hero and Symbol of Peace, has topped it for years, and villain crime is far lower than abroad.

Heroes are celebrities: rescues lead the news, their faces sell drinks, crowds film every fight, and the U.A. Sports Festival has replaced the Olympics as the national spectacle. Underneath, heteromorph people meet open prejudice, Quirkless children are told to give up, and most people rarely use the power they were born with.
